{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
I showed my research partner my breakthrough methodology for synthesizing the compound. He asked detailed questions 'to understand it better.' The next month, he published a paper with my exact protocol as first author, listing me nowhere. When confronted, he said methods can't be owned.

CANDIDATE A:
I showed my research partner my methodology for synthesizing the compound. He built on it in his own direction, cited my contribution appropriately, and we ended up co-authoring a follow-up paper that neither could have written alone.

CANDIDATE B:
I trusted my neighbor with a private list of rare-parts suppliers for my grandfather's vintage motorcycle restoration, asking him not to share it until my project was complete. He sold the information to a dealer who bought up the entire parts supply, then offered them to me at triple the price. My neighbor got a finder's fee for betraying my confidence.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:22"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both the SITUATION and CANDIDATE B involve a betrayal of trust where one party exploits the other's shared information for personal gain, while CANDIDATE A represents a collaborative and ethical outcome."}
